note:
Repair the bottle wording on SERUMS-R2-A-FOREARM seedream_01, which Malcolm picked off ~/Desktop/skingenetix-SERUMS-R2-A-FOREARM.png and reported as 'not correct and not clear'.

THE FAULT, read at 100%. Same product as the fine-lines banner, far worse execution: five of the six label elements are wrong. 'ACETYL' prints as ACETVL with the Y drawn as a V; 'ANTI-WRINKLE' as ANTI-JVAINUE; 'SERUM' as SEIUII; 'PREMIUM FORMULA' as FRONIUM FOMULA; and the concentration line is illegible. Only the 'Skingenetix' wordmark is clean, and the helix mark is drawn as a thick solid form rather than the dots and dashes the brand mark actually uses.

SO THIS IS A LEGIBILITY FAILURE, NOT A CONTENT ONE — the lines are all present and all of them are mangled. That is the opposite of the fine-lines banner, where the lines rendered were correct and two were simply absent. Same repair brief serves both, because it pins every element AND states the letterforms that drift.

SEEDREAM DREW THIS ONE, so the repair deliberately goes to all four suppliers rather than back to the engine that produced the fault. On this project gpt-image solved MATRIXYL first attempt after Seedream failed it in ~30 of 50 candidates; the failure modes do not overlap.

The prompt holds face, pose, lighting, framing and hand constant by name — an edit prompt that mentions only the fix invites a restage.

slots.title: SERUMS-R2-A-FOREARM seedream_01 — redraw the bottle wording legibly
slots.prompt: Reproduce the first reference photograph exactly as it is. Keep the identical composition, the identical pose, the identical model and her face unchanged, the identical camera angle and framing, the identical lighting, shadows and background, and the identical position, size and angle of the hand and the bottle it holds. Change ONLY the wording printed on the bottle. The bottle itself stays exactly as it is: a 30ml frosted clear glass dropper bottle, straight-sided with square shoulders, a brushed satin silver collar and a white rubber-bulb pipette, holding a clear colourless water-transparent serum — the frosting is the glass, not the contents. Print the label exactly as the second reference shows it, as five stacked elements, centred as a block on the front of the glass: first a fine double helix drawn as small dots and dashes, never a solid ribbon or swirl; below it the wordmark 'Skingenetix' with a capital S and the rest lower case; below that, in black capitals on two lines, 'ACETYL' then 'HEXAPEPTIDE-8', with a hyphen before the digit 8; below that, in soft grey capitals on two lines, 'ANTI-WRINKLE' then 'SERUM', where ANTI-WRINKLE begins with the letter W; below that, in smaller grey capitals, 'PREMIUM FORMULA'; and last, as a single fine line of small grey capitals, '10% ACETYL HEXAPEPTIDE-8 | 30ML'. A slim vertical rule sits to the left of those lines and stops level with the last of them. EVERY LINE MUST BE SHARP AND FULLY LEGIBLE, printed crisply on the glass and readable letter by letter. The version being corrected rendered all six elements as mangled approximations - ACETVL for ACETYL, ANTI-JVAINUE for ANTI-WRINKLE, SEIUII for SERUM, FRONIUM FOMULA for PREMIUM FORMULA - so the letterforms matter as much as the wording. Every one of the six elements above must be present, correctly spelled and cleanly drawn. Add nothing else to the bottle: no other words, no numbers, no symbols, no registered or trademark marks.
